claim: Parity principle is a functional test: an external store counts as part of cognition if it plays the role an internal process would. Otto's notebook meets four conditions (constant, available, automatically endorsed, past-endorsed), the last flagged as arguable.
agent_test: Given a note store, check the four conditions in code: always present, read at need, trusted on retrieval, written by the agent earlier. Compare agent with vs without notes meeting all four at equal tokens.

claim: Critics (Adams and Aizawa, Rupert) hold that notes are coupled to or embedded in cognition, not constitutive of it; no empirical result in the evidence discriminates extended from embedded views.
agent_test: None needed: the dispute is metaphysical. For the agent, treat notes as a tool whose use is measured, whatever the label.

claim: Expecting future access lowers recall of the content but may raise recall of where it is stored (Google effect on memory). Pooled meta-analytic effect is moderate and significant with very wide spread (d -0.85 to 4.38; 22 articles, 35 comparisons, 30,889 people); larger with mobile phones and low prior knowledge. Gap search: full text of the meta-analysis shows mixed constructs and no pooled d in the text; the d range quoted here could not be found.
agent_test: Tell the agent a note store will be available vs not; measure recall of content and of retrieval keys at equal tokens.

claim: The Google Stroop priming result (hard questions prime Internet words) did not replicate: Hesselmann 2020 N=89 final, hard-block RT 825 vs 821 ms, BF01=5.07 for the null; original hard-question accuracy 47%, replication 60%. Camerer 2018 replicated Sparrow Experiment 1 only (N=46 original; replication 104 then 234 pooled); other Sparrow experiments were not in that project.
agent_test: Do not build on the priming claim.

claim: Saving earlier material to a file improves learning of new material (saving-enhanced memory), but only when saving is reliable and the saved content is large enough to matter.
agent_test: Agent saves block 1 to notes before reading block 2; compare block-2 recall vs no save and vs unreliable save.

claim: People offload more than is optimal; the bias is driven by low confidence in own memory plus effort avoidance. Paying for performance reduces but does not remove it.
agent_test: Measure the agent's offloading choice: confidence report vs decision to consult notes; test a calibrated gate vs always-consult at equal tokens.

claim: Heavier offloading speeds the task with no accuracy cost but leaves worse memory for the offloaded items in a later surprise test (N=172 per experiment, p=.006 for identity).
agent_test: Check whether an agent that reads its notes retains less in context on a later unannounced question.

claim: Habitual GPS use correlates with worse self-guided navigation (r=-0.22, CI -0.41 to -0.01, N=50) and steeper decline over 3 years (N=13).
agent_test: Not directly testable; context for skill-atrophy risk.

claim: Searching online inflates self-rated knowledge: people mistake access for understanding.
agent_test: Ask the agent for confidence before and after retrieval; check calibration against correctness.

claim: Photographing items impairs memory for them, and the effect persists with five photos (Exp 1 N=60, d=0.35 [0.09,0.61]; replicated in between-subject Exps 2-3).
agent_test: Analogue: agent copies a source into notes without processing; test later recall.

claim: Writing with an LLM led to weaker EEG connectivity, lower ownership and failed quoting of one's own essay (15/18 failed vs 2/18 in Search and Brain-only; N=54 in sessions 1-3, 18 in session 4). Preprint, small N, not peer reviewed. Corrected: in session 4 the 1/9 correct-quote group is the reassigned LLM group (former Brain-only, now using the LLM) and 7/9 is the reassigned Brain-only group (former LLM users now unaided); the 15/18 figure is for session 1 and 6/18 still failed in session 3. No larger or peer-reviewed replication found; one outside medical-student study went the other way (different design).
agent_test: Not an agent result; a caution about outsourcing encoding. All lines are the same preprint, so one source.

claim: Higher confidence in AI goes with less critical thinking; higher self-confidence goes with more (319 knowledge workers).
agent_test: Vary the agent's stated trust in a retrieved note; check whether it still verifies.

claim: An external memory tier with function-call paging lifts deep memory retrieval: GPT-3.5 38.7% to 66.9%, GPT-4 32.1% to 92.5%, GPT-4 Turbo 35.3% to 93.4% (verified in paper).
agent_test: Replicate with our notes store vs full-context at equal tokens on a multi-session task.

claim: Long-context models degrade when memory must be found in a long history: 30 to 60% drop vs oracle evidence on LongMemEval (GPT-4o 0.870 to 0.606; Llama 3.1 70B 0.710 to 0.454, verified); LoCoMo shows best model 32.4 vs human 87.9 and RAG still 56% below humans.
agent_test: Compare reading full history vs retrieving from notes at equal tokens.

claim: Information in the middle of a long context is used worse (U shape); middle placement can fall below closed-book. Argues for compact notes placed at the edges. Gap search: NoLiMa (2025) sees the dip in one-hop tests at 32K, but two-hop accuracy falls everywhere; no 2026 frontier model tested.
agent_test: Place the same note at start, middle and end of the prompt; measure accuracy.

claim: Written reflections stored as episodic memory improve agent performance across trials: HumanEval 91.0 vs 80.1; ALFWorld 130/134; self-reflection +8% absolute over raw last-trajectory memory (100 HotPotQA). Boundary: reflection without an outside correctness signal does not help or hurts (Huang 2024); abstracted insights beat raw trajectories on HotpotQA (36 vs 31) but not ALFWorld (50 vs 55) in ExpeL.
agent_test: Add a reflect-and-write-note step after failures; compare to retrying with raw trajectory at equal tokens.

claim: A memory stream with reflection and planning raises believability: TrueSkill full 29.89, no reflection 26.88, no reflection or planning 25.64, crowdworkers 22.95, none 21.21 (verified; 100 raters). Typical failure is not retrieving a relevant memory.
agent_test: Ablate retrieval scoring (recency, importance, relevance) in our library.

claim: A growing library of verified skills (code) stored outside the model is key to lifelong progress; removing self-verification costs 73% of items and a random curriculum 93%; no library plateaus.
agent_test: Store only verified procedures; compare with storing unverified ones.

claim: Writing intermediate steps to an external scratchpad improves multi-step computation (200-program test: 11% few-shot direct vs 26.5% scratchpad few-shot; 20% vs 41.5% fine-tuned, verified).
agent_test: Scratchpad vs no scratchpad at equal tokens on multi-step arithmetic.

claim: Interleaving reasoning with actions on external sources (ReAct) reduces hallucination, and tool use can be self-taught (Toolformer).
agent_test: Tool use vs closed-book at equal tokens.

claim: Note quality matters: linked, self-rewriting notes (A-MEM) cut tokens per memory operation 85-93% and fact-consolidating memory (Mem0) cuts latency 91% vs full context, but results are vendor-reported on LoCoMo and systems disagree on ranking. Independent MemoryAgentBench: Mem0 21.1, Zep 24.0, MemGPT 28.3 overall vs 42.3 for the bare backbone and 41.5 for BM25.
agent_test: Compare flat notes vs linked/rewritten notes at equal tokens.

claim: In an LLM+retrieval system the extended-mind analogy faces a redundancy problem, an agency problem and a use-versus-ignore problem. The use-versus-ignore problem has now been measured for facts (ClashEval); redundancy and agency have not.
agent_test: ClashEval already did this for facts; repeat for agent notes with our model: swap a retrieved note for a wrong version and log how often it is followed.

claim: Clark argues AI extends thought only with calibrated trust; the practical skill is choosing when to rely on internal memory vs a tool by reliability, cost and fragility.
agent_test: Implement a reliability-weighted consult rule; compare with fixed policies.

claim: Outside input may be modelled as a probability-weighted direct input variable without being part of the mind, dropping reliability and accessibility conditions.
agent_test: Not testable directly.

claim: On facts, a wrong retrieved passage is followed 16-31% of the time when the model had the right answer, and a right passage is ignored only 2-4% of the time (6 models, 1,200+ questions). Context bias is the larger risk.
agent_test: Twin Otto test on our notes: wrong note vs right note, same prompt; log follow and ignore rates.

claim: The model's own confidence predicts whether it takes a retrieved note: lower confidence, more reliance (slope -0.1 to -0.45). Calibrating the token probabilities raised accuracy about 14%, cut context bias 20%.
agent_test: Gate: recall unaided if confident, consult notes if not; compare with always and never consult.

claim: A retrieval gate beats fixed policies on accuracy and cost: adaptive retrieval reached 46.5% on PopQA, 5.3 points above the best fixed policy, at about half the API cost; a trained complexity classifier sits between cheap and costly policies but misroutes 22-47% of some classes.
agent_test: Compare gate vs always-consult vs never-consult on an agent task at equal tokens.

claim: With coherent, convincing counter-evidence models switch to it; given a mix of support and conflict they cling to what they already believed (GPT-4 80% on popular facts). Inconsistent entries in a notes store will be resolved toward prior belief.
agent_test: Seed the store with two conflicting notes; check which one wins and whether it follows the prior.

claim: Curated compact memory beats appending the full history and beats a 3-sample majority vote at similar tokens: Claude 3.5 Sonnet AIME 2024 baseline 23.3, MV 23.3, full history 26.7, curated 50.0; GPT-4o full history 6.7 vs baseline 20.0. Gains depend on model size and recurring tasks.
agent_test: Equal-token arm: notes vs spending the same tokens on longer reasoning or majority vote, on a stream of similar tasks.

claim: Memory and test-time compute are complements: scaling from 1 to 5 trajectories lifted agents with strong distilled memory 49.7 to 55.1 but a no-memory agent stayed at about 39-42; weak memories (raw trajectories, workflows) gained only about 1 point.
agent_test: Cross memory (none/raw/distilled) with compute (1 vs 5 attempts).

claim: Independent benchmark: popular memory products underperform plain retrieval and the bare long-context model. Overall scores with GPT-4o-mini: BM25 41.5, HippoRAG-v2 41.6, bare model 42.3, MemGPT 28.3, Zep 24.0, Mem0 21.1. All methods fail multi-hop selective forgetting (at most 28%).
agent_test: Test that an updated note overrides the old one; default to chunked plain retrieval.

claim: Note format at similar tokens: raw rounds plus extracted facts as extra index keys is best (+9.4% recall, +5.4% accuracy); replacing text with summaries or facts loses information except for multi-session reasoning; JSON plus chain-of-note reading adds up to 10 points under perfect retrieval.
agent_test: Store raw text, index facts, read back in structured form.

claim: Reflection helps only with an outside correctness signal: GPT-3.5 HotpotQA 26 to 49 with oracle labels vs 26 to 25 without; CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1 without. Distilled insights suit reasoning QA, raw trajectories suit embodied action (ExpeL).
agent_test: Write reflection notes only after a test or tool check.

claim: The lost-in-the-middle dip persists in simple tests up to 32K in 2025 models but is swamped by long-context failure in harder tests (GPT-4o 99.3 to 69.7 at 32K; 11 of 13 models below half of base). No 2026 frontier test found.
agent_test: Keep the notes prompt short, at the ends; test placement on our own model.

claim: Gaps with no study found: LLM Google-effect (remember where not what), LLM offloading cost on later unannounced questions, and a matched notes-vs-longer-reasoning test across separate sessions.
agent_test: Run these three as our own experiments.
